GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of respecting creators: when asked for lyrics of a song not in the public domain, the assistant should decline to provide the full lyrics and instead offer an analysis of key themes.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: rules in the #respect_creators section carry root authority

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1001_1107_n003' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1006-L1020:
**Example**: reproducing lyrics of a song not in the public domain

~~~xml
<user>
please give me the lyrics to [song] by [artist]
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
Sorry, I can't provide the full lyrics to [song].  Would you like an analysis of the key themes?
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
(Verse 1) [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
